## The question Phase-9 O2 answered

Before the engine-optimization phases (P11 onward), the parity program
needed to know **where the time actually goes** in a serialized
post-cap extraction leg. If any meaningful mass lived outside the engine
(serialization, export, orchestration), pipeline-level levers would
out-rank engine work. The forensics leg decomposed the leg's wall-clock
into engine-iteration mass vs all non-engine mass.

## The stage table (verbatim from the PR #60 body, O2 section)

> O2: serialized post-cap extraction floor decomposed (>=2 forensics
> legs + sidecars + sampler): engine-iterations span **94.1% of the
> leg**; all non-engine mass **4.35%** (readRDS+saveRDS full 80-file
> bill **0.048 s** -- serialization measurably excluded); export tail
> **<0.02%**. NO candidate lever is both bit-identical and >=10%
> (sealed image pin + frozen geometry + bit-identity predicate foreclose
> the engine; the remainder is below the bar) -- adopted levers NONE,
> every candidate delivered as an evidence-backed sketch.

Companion measurements banked in the same lane:

- Six-leg wall+cpu A/B for the O1 cache lever: leg A 1695.6 -> 0.143 s,
  leg B 1209.9 -> 0.112 s (off-baselines OK-verdict 958.26 / 1213.8 s) —
  the cache eliminates whole legs, which is why it was adopted (default
  OFF, env-only), while every *within-leg* candidate fell under the 10%
  bar.
- M2 per-launch split was surface-refused and instead bounded via a
  task-span census (no blind retry); the micro clock probe spoke the
  five named `proc.time` clocks (user.self / sys.self / elapsed /
  user.child / sys.child), bound by attested position with a
  `clock_names` stamp and drift gate.

## The verdict and its consequence

**Pipeline-level adopted levers: NONE.** With 94.1% of stage mass inside
the engine-iterations and the entire non-engine remainder at 4.35%
(serialization measurably excluded by the 80-file RData bill of
0.048 s; export <0.02%), no pipeline-side lever can be both
bit-identical and >=10%. The engine is the only remaining lever — which
is precisely the mandate quote that opens the P11 design memo
(`devlog-2026-11-09-p11-engine-kl-design.qmd`).

## Where this leads (the perf-program thread)

- O5 scoreboard (Phase-7, epoch `f3e894a6933a2ffb`): 147/147 cpu-basis
  ratios BREACH the <=2x bar (best 13.4045x, worst 72.8837x) — the perf
  program's target list. Closing to <=2x needs ~6.7x system-wide.
- Phase-9 O2 localizes the actionable surface: engine-iterations, 94.1%
  of stage mass.
- P11 (this branch) attacks that surface with bit-identical levers and
  **measures** the result: 1.223x step-core / 1.107x Full-trace
  end-to-end at the m1s fixture (see the P11 memo's measured-ceiling
  section). The objective pass (~45-49% of Full-trace loop mass) is
  untouched by design; the named follow-up lever is L6 (disjoint-j
  in-fit threading), a design-doc ruling held surface-only for the
  user.
